newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HALTS ENERGY PRICE HIKES THIS WINTER.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HALTS ENERGY PRICE HIKES THIS WINTER.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet has frozen current energy prices for this winter amid protests of ordinary Bulgarians against drastic increases, the cabinet press centre said on Thursday.

Under the pricing mechanism, since July energy prices have been revised each month mainly according to the inflation rate and the lev/dollar exchange rate. But rising prices of electricity, coal and central heating are choking the economy and the overstretched budgets of ordinary Bulgarians.
Last week Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov withdrew his proposal for a fresh energy price rise next month after Deputy Prime Minister Roumen Gechev opposed the ministry's energy pricing system.
Energy officials said international lending institutions had recommended a target electricity rate of 3.5 cents per kilowatt hour, while it was currently less than three cents.
Ovcharov has said a chronic shortage of cash for the energy sector would create problems at the beginning next year.
